SERMON TEXTS WHERE THE IRV READS DIFFERENTLY and Spurgeon's argument needs the KJV sense (the key phrase is our own rendering, recorded self_rendered; the rest of the verse is IRV): ch16 Amos 2:13 'I am pressed under you' — the IRV reads मैं तुम को ऐसा दबाऊँगा ('I will press you'), which is the alternative reading Spurgeon himself mentions; ch08 Isa 28:25 'the principal wheat' (मुख्य गेहूँ) — the IRV has गेहूँ को पाँति-पाँति ('wheat in rows'), again the alternative Spurgeon cites in his section IV.

Other KJV/IRV divergences an editor should see (IRV kept inside the quotation marks): Gen 6:3 निवास न करेगा for 'strive' (ch06); Isa 28:24 लगातार for 'all day' (ch05 refrain); Ps 119:113 दुचित्तों for 'vain thoughts', Eph 6:14 no 'stand' (ch02, self); Zech 3:2 अपना लेता है for 'chosen' (ch02); Mark 9:23 opening (ch03); Ps 147:17-18 no 'his' (ch03); Ps 65:10 'the springing thereof' = उसकी उपज (ch09 refrain); Gen 49:10 no 'gathering of the people' (ch18); Matt 13:30 IRV और where Spurgeon builds on 'but' (ch18 carries परन्तु in narration only); Isa 53:1 without 'Lord,' (ch07); Eph 1:6 no 'accepted' (ch15, self). John 12:23's IRV typo 'पुत्र कि महिमा' is written की (ch04, recorded adapted).

Conventions: curly quotation marks mirror the English per chapter; the reader addressed as तुम, God in prayer as तू (a few one-to-one appeals — 'young man', 'soul' — also तू, IRV style); Christ in the singular; farm vocabulary from the IRV (हल जोतनेवाला, सिला बीनना, दाँवना, खत्ता, पूला, कठिया गेहूँ for rye); section numerals I., II. mirror the English; chapter titles pinned across all translators.
